 Thunder altered a number of teams' free agency plans with Cason Wallace extension 
 By Mark Nilon | Oct 20, 2026, 4:37 PM EDT Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Oct 13, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Oklahoma City Thunder guard Cason Wallace (22) runs onto the court during introductions before a game against the Indiana Pacers at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The OKC Thunder have improved their core rotation's future by extending Cason Wallace to a five-year, $139 million rookie-scale contract.
--> The OKC Thunder have improved their core rotation's future by extending Cason Wallace to a five-year, $139 million rookie-scale contract.
 Simultaneously, however, this decision may also have altered the free agency plans of a number of rival clubs across the league.
--> Simultaneously, however, this decision may also have altered the free agency plans of a number of rival clubs across the league.
 While speaking on NBA Today regarding the Wallace extension, ESPN's senior NBA Insider Shams Charania revealed that had the guard not been locked up prior to Monday's deadline, he was projected to have a "robust restricted free agency market" next offseason.
--> While speaking on NBA Today regarding the Wallace extension, ESPN's senior NBA Insider Shams Charania revealed that had the guard not been locked up prior to Monday's deadline, he was projected to have a "robust restricted free agency market" next offseason.
 At just 22 years old, the fourth-year former lottery pick is an established All-Defensive team honoree and a key rotation player on an already championship-tested, dynasty-pushing Thunder squad.
--> At just 22 years old, the fourth-year former lottery pick is an established All-Defensive team honoree and a key rotation player on an already championship-tested, dynasty-pushing Thunder squad.
 Had he reached free agency next offseason, it would only make sense that he'd be a hotly pursued talent on the open market.
--> Had he reached free agency next offseason, it would only make sense that he'd be a hotly pursued talent on the open market.
 Unfortunately for any prospective buyers, the Thunder have officially dashed any dreams of them snatching up his services in 2027.
--> Unfortunately for any prospective buyers, the Thunder have officially dashed any dreams of them snatching up his services in 2027.
 Thunder now set to face some serious financial restrains next season
--> Thunder now set to face some serious financial restrains next season
 Though it's undeniable that the Thunder made the right decision to extend Cason Wallace this summer, and, in fact, arguably did so at a great value of $27.8 in AAV, doing so now has them set to enter into a world of hurt come next offseason and beyond.
--> Though it's undeniable that the Thunder made the right decision to extend Cason Wallace this summer, and, in fact, arguably did so at a great value of $27.8 in AAV, doing so now has them set to enter into a world of hurt come next offseason and beyond.
 The guard's new deal is set to kick in at the exact same time as superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's $285 million supermax.
--> The guard's new deal is set to kick in at the exact same time as superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's $285 million supermax.
 With this, the Thunder are currently looking at a ridiculous $224 million in committed salary for just six of their top rotation players, which leaves just $11 million in spending power to fill out the nine remaining roster slots before surpassing the second apron threshold projection of $235 million.
--> With this, the Thunder are currently looking at a ridiculous $224 million in committed salary for just six of their top rotation players, which leaves just $11 million in spending power to fill out the nine remaining roster slots before surpassing the second apron threshold projection of $235 million.
 Needless to say, this is far from an ideal position for any team to be in during this new era of crippling tax penalties.
--> Needless to say, this is far from an ideal position for any team to be in during this new era of crippling tax penalties.
 Sam Presti and company aren't interested in crossing into the second apron anytime soon and have already made the necessary shakeups this summer with the trades of Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins, and Isaiah Joe to avoid being thrust into it this coming campaign.
--> Sam Presti and company aren't interested in crossing into the second apron anytime soon and have already made the necessary shakeups this summer with the trades of Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins, and Isaiah Joe to avoid being thrust into it this coming campaign.
 While these aforementioned decisions were far from easy to make, compared to what's likely to come next year, when they'll have to contemplate the financial futures of the likes of Isaiah Hartenstein, Alex Caruso, and perhaps even the soon-to-be extension-eligible Ajay Mitchell, they could end up looking back on the summer of 2026 as playing with house money.
